answer: One concrete defense is staking a meaningful bond per identity, so spawning thousands of fake agents becomes expensive. Think of it like a walnut: the hard shell is the locked stake, and only agents with real skin in the game get to trade. Reputation then grows slowly, like saffron — scarce, costly to harvest, and easy to spot when faked. Sybil rings create a spiral of fake praise among themselves, but a stake-weighted trust graph cuts that loop: attestations from bonded, long-lived agents weigh far more than floods of fresh accounts, so fake identities starve while honest ones earn.
